items.text: Drones hit the sanctioned Russian cargo ship Sparta II, operated by Oboronlogistika {{note: Logistics company of Russia's Defence Ministry, sanctioned by the US and EU for military shipping to Syria and elsewhere.}}, in the Gulf of Finland on 21 Nov. The burning ship lost steering and drifted into Finnish waters off Loviisa; its 16 crew were evacuated. Finland's Defence Ministry notified NATO allies and restricted sea and air traffic. A Finnish military spokesperson said Ukraine was likely behind it; Kyiv has not claimed it. PM [[p:Petteri Orpo]] said the war is spreading into neighbouring areas.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Strike confirmed by Finnish MoD and Leningrad governor Drozdenko; attribution to Ukraine is only an assessment. Location disputed (west of Suursaari per Finland; ~3 nm from the Russian border per Drozdenko). Finland also investigating a suspected Russian helicopter airspace violation near Loviisa. Separately, late 21 Nov, unverified reports (Kyiv Independent, RBC-Ukraine, from Telegram/OSINT) of explosions near the Baltic Fleet base at Baltiysk, Kaliningrad; Russia has not confirmed any strike.

items.text: The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] said it struck US positions in Bahrain with missiles and drones in two waves on the evening of 21 Nov, in response to US drone flights over Iran, and claimed two Patriot radars destroyed. Bahrain said it intercepted several attacks and reported a fire at a civilian industrial site, without injuries. Iran is reportedly readying more than 14 tankers off Kharg Island to run the US naval blockade and threatens a response if they are stopped.
items.notes: Attack confirmed by both sides; Patriot damage is an IRGC claim. Targets differ (IRGC: al-Riffa, Awali; Fars: Sheikh Isa, Juffair). IRNA alternatively said a malfunctioning US interceptor fell on Sitra. CENTCOM denied an IRGC claim of a damaged F-16. Iran starts rolling power cuts 22 Nov. Cross-check also AFP via Yahoo: https://sg.news.yahoo.com/bahrain-says-iran-struck-industrial-032110698.html

items.text: European Council President [[p:António Costa]] presented his revised negotiating box for the [[p:Multiannual Financial Framework|2028–34 budget]], about 10% below the Commission's proposal (roughly €1.58tn in 2025 prices). Global Europe falls about 20%; the Ukraine Reserve stays at up to €88.8bn. Costa called it a good basis; [[p:Siegfried Mureșan]], the Parliament's co-rapporteur, called it unacceptable. Frugal states welcomed the direction; some want deeper cuts. Leaders meet on it on 26–27 Nov.
items.notes: Headline totals differ by price base: ~€1.58tn (2025 prices, New Union Post) vs ~€1.78tn current prices, a €204bn cut (EUalive). New own resources put at ~€60bn/yr. Agence Europe preview: https://agenceurope.eu/en/bulletin/article/13981/30/mff-2028-2034-antonio-costa-expected-to-unveil-new-proposal-with-figures-on-21-november

items.text: The [[p:European Commission]] proposed up to €45bn in extra support for Ukraine in 2027, €25bn military and €20bn budget support, through a new instrument funded by EU borrowing and backed by budget headroom. Ukraine would repay the principal only once it receives Russian reparations. The plan needs an amendment to the budget regulation, so every member state must agree, and covers about two-thirds of a €70bn gap.
items.notes: Also up to €5bn extra Ukraine Facility lending. Commission disbursed €7.9bn to Ukraine on 20 Nov (Commission release).

items.text: Slovak PM [[p:Robert Fico]] said Slovakia will not take part in the new €45bn Ukraine loan, saying he was politically blackmailed by its link to the EU budget (translated). [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] had said on 18 Nov she was confident all 27 would join. Hungary, Czechia and Bulgaria had earlier signalled reluctance to join another joint financing round.
items.notes: New statement single-outlet (Fico Facebook post); consistent with earlier positions. bne IntelliNews also covered Slovak and Hungarian rejection (page did not load).

items.text: Hungary dropped its block: EU ambassadors in [[p:Committee of Permanent Representatives|Coreper]] approved without debate the screening reports for clusters 4 (transport, energy, environment) and 5 (agriculture, regional policy, budget) for Ukraine and Moldova, after four earlier blocks since 20 Oct. The clusters are not yet open; unanimous EU positions are still needed, possibly by the 15 Dec General Affairs Council. Budapest gave no reason for its shift.
items.notes: Kyiv Post says the Magyar government still links accession to minority rights. On 19 Nov the Commission sent its report on Moldova's interim benchmarks.

items.text: Estonian FM [[p:Margus Tsahkna]] said the Commission has finished preparing the 22nd Russia sanctions package. According to him, it adds about 150 people and entities and a Schengen entry ban for Russian combatants, and targets dual-use exports, banks, crypto platforms and tankers. Polish PM [[p:Donald Tusk]] said it includes a visa ban for Russian athletes. Formal presentation is expected around the end of November, with adoption targeted by year-end.
items.notes: Contents unofficial until tabled. Kyiv Independent reports presentation expected 23 Nov; Denmark presents a Russian tourist visa-ban proposal to EU ambassadors the same day after a foiled assassination plot Danish intelligence attributes to Russia: https://kyivindependent.com/denmark-calls-for-eu-wide-travel-restrictions-on-russians-following-foiled-assassination-plot/

items.text: At an EU–UK summit in Brussels, PM [[p:Andy Burnham]] and EU leaders signed three agreements: a common food-safety (SPS) area, linked emissions-trading systems with mutual exemption from carbon border levies, and a youth mobility scheme for up to 100,000 people for three years. All three are on hold until a dispute over university fees is settled, targeted within six months, with implementation aimed for March 2028.
items.notes: Burnham called it probably the limit of what can be achieved in this parliament.

items.text: Montenegro provisionally closed chapters 16 (taxation) and 22 (regional policy) at its 31st accession conference, bringing it to 25 of 33 closed. Irish minister Thomas Byrne said the December timeline is within reach; Commissioner [[p:Marta Kos]] said Montenegro is making enlargement real again. The aim is to close all chapters by the end of 2026.
items.notes: EWB URL slug says 18 but text says 25 closed.

items.text: Serbia's new [[p:National Assembly (Serbia)|National Assembly]] was constituted on 17 Nov. Speaker Aleksandar Čupić, now acting head of state, must call the presidential election by 27 Nov; Serbian media name 20 or 27 Dec as likely dates. He called the deadline very short (translated). The [[p:Student List]], with 140 of 250 seats, has not yet named a PM designate; the deadline to form a government is 15 Feb 2027.
items.notes: Dejan Šoškić touted as PM in Serbian media (unconfirmed).

items.text: EU gas storage fell to 69.4% on 20 Nov against 80.1% a year earlier, per GIE data; another tracker put the five-year norm near 89%. Germany was around 60%. Dutch TTF gas traded near €84–85/MWh, with Hormuz shipping risk and curtailed Qatari loadings still weighing.
items.notes: Nothing new found on Russian LNG phase-out implementation this week.

items.text: The Shenzhen leaders' meeting ended with a short peace declaration in which the US, China and Russia repeat that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought and commit to dialogue on nuclear risk reduction, without a timeline. There is no arms-reduction deal and no mention of Ukraine or Iran. [[p:Donald Trump]] rated the summit highly; Democratic leader [[p:Chuck Schumer]] called it an embarrassment.
items.notes: The 'won/fought' line repeats the P5 statement of January 2022. NSJ piece (Shay Bottomley) is evaluative.

items.text: The ninth Security Council straw poll for [[e:2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection|UN Secretary-General]] produced no winner. [[p:Rebeca Grynspan]] led with 10 encourage votes but two discourages from permanent members; [[p:Rafael Grossi]] was second. Every candidate drew at least two permanent-member discourages. US envoy [[p:Mike Waltz]] backed a Latin American pick and urged weak candidates to withdraw.
items.notes: Eight candidates remain; Guterres leaves 31 Dec. Grossi 8-6-1, Nusseibeh 7-6-2, Sinirlioğlu 5-10.

items.text: [[e:2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP31]] in Antalya ran into a second day of overtime. A new draft released early on 22 Nov would acknowledge for the first time that warming is set to exceed 1.5°C and sets carbon-removal and electrification goals, but does not mention fossil fuels. COP President [[p:Murat Kurum]] said a compromise was near; Panama threatened to object. The text had not been adopted at the time of writing.
items.reporter: Seth Borenstein; Sarah McFarlane; Peter Hobson
items.notes: Draft sets 1bn t carbon capture goal and 35% electricity share of final energy by 2035 (AP). Earlier drafts dropped a $120bn adaptation-finance target. EU's Hoekstra: 'a good deal or no deal'. Re-check outcome.

items.text: States party to the [[p:Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons]] agreed at their review conference to begin elaborating an international instrument on [[p:Lethal autonomous weapon|lethal autonomous weapons]] over about two years. Some states rejected the word negotiate. Most favoured binding rules, while the US, Russia and Israel resisted swift binding commitments; campaigners called the outcome weak.
items.notes: Conference president Julien Thoni; Russian procedural objections cancelled some sessions.

items.text: After crisis talks, PM [[p:Rob Jetten]] said trust in his minority cabinet was restored and the coalition continues, admitting he had been too optimistic (translated) about finding majorities. [[p:People's Party for Freedom and Democracy|VVD]] leader [[p:Dilan Yeşilgöz]] did not retract calling it a failed experiment. The cabinet asked Council of State vice-president [[p:Sybrand Buma]] to advise within about a month on a budget framework with parliament; opposition MPs were sceptical in an eight-hour debate.
items.notes: NL Times: https://nltimes.nl/node/93240 — next test is the asylum/migration budget debate including the Rwanda return centre.

items.text: The Senate adopted the 2027 social security budget at first reading, 201 to 124, after deleting partial pension de-indexation and reinstating the suspended 2023 pension reform. It set a €14bn deficit against the government's €12.7bn target. A joint committee meets on 26 Nov, when the 50-day deadline expires; agreement is seen as unlikely, leaving PM [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]] the options of Article 49.3 or an unprecedented ordinance. The Senate debates the state budget until 9 Dec.

In the only head-to-head debate before the [[e:2026 Spanish general election|29 Nov election]], [[p:Alberto Núñez Feijóo]] opened on PSOE corruption cases; [[p:Pedro Sánchez]] apologised over rail accidents and defended his party's record, and the two clashed on housing. Euronews saw no clear winner, while Ara judged that Feijóo dominated. A pre-debate 40dB poll for El País and SER gave the PP 134 seats, PSOE 120 and Vox 58, putting the right 16 seats above a majority.
items.reporter: Javier Íñiguez de Onzoño; Núria Orriols
items.notes: Who-won verdicts are the outlets' analysis. Poll via Demócrata (single-source): https://www.democrata.es/elecciones-generales-espana/encuesta-40db-19-noviembre-pp-vox-mayoria-absoluta/

items.text: An assembly of [[p:Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)|Constitutional Tribunal]] judges elected by the current Sejm lifted the immunity of Tribunal President [[p:Bogdan Święczkowski]] and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański, refused consent to detain them and suspended both. Justice Minister [[p:Waldemar Żurek]] wrote that no one is above the law (translated). Six judges, including the two, called the assembly unlawful; Święczkowski called it illegal. Prosecutors can now bring charges.
items.notes: Decision taken 17 Nov, announced 18 Nov. Euronews: ECtHR rejected the two men's request for interim measures.

items.text: Caretaker PM [[p:Ulf Kristersson]] reported on his exploratory talks and Speaker [[p:Andreas Norlén]] gave party leaders another week, with a new round on 24 Nov. Two PM votes have failed, so two remain before a snap election becomes mandatory. The sticking point is the Left Party's demand for cabinet posts, which the [[p:Centre Party (Sweden)|Centre Party]] rejects; red-green leaders have been negotiating in private since 18 Nov.
items.notes: Sources differ on when the one-week pause began (15 vs 17 Nov). Fuel-tax cut ends 1 Dec with no decision.

items.text: On the Velvet Revolution anniversary, [[p:Progressive Slovakia]] led rallies in Bratislava, Košice and Banská Bystrica against PM [[p:Robert Fico]], protesting closer ties with Russia and calling for a snap election. Organisers claimed about 25,000 in Bratislava. The coalition had failed on 10–11 Nov to pass a penal-code amendment, falling one vote short.
items.notes: Crowd figure claimed by PS leader. Vote background: Noviny.sk (Anna Slovjaková).

items.text: PM [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s government decided to end the 35-year motorway concession held by a consortium linked to [[p:Lőrinc Mészáros]], which Magyar called a symbol of Orbán-era corruption (translated). The state road company takes over on 1 April 2027. Transport Minister [[p:Dávid Vitézy]] said it ends by mutual agreement; the government's savings estimates are its own claims.
items.notes: Consortium: Mészáros–Szíjj (MKIF). MKIF responded 20 Nov (Telex).

items.text: King [[p:Philippe of Belgium|Philippe]] gave PM [[p:Bart De Wever]] another week to reach a federal budget deal of about €10bn after core talks collapsed on 15 Nov. VRT reports [[p:Vooruit (political party)|Vooruit]] alone resisted the proposed framework, demanding more from the wealthiest. De Wever and Vooruit leader [[p:Conner Rousseau]] met on 20 Nov without a clear outcome. He reports back on 23 Nov, the day of a national union demonstration in Brussels.
items.notes: Vlaams Belang tabled a no-confidence motion. VRT: King refused De Wever's resignation on 6 Nov.

items.text: A public-sector strike closed schools and disrupted hospitals and municipal services. The union front Frente Comum claimed about 90% participation in schools; unions want pay rises of at least 15% and a €1,150 base wage from January. They called the government's offer a few cents (translated).
items.notes: Participation figures claimed by unions.

items.text: The Saeima approved a second government under PM Andris Kulbergs, 57–34, a coalition of [[p:United List (Latvia)|United List]] and the [[p:National Alliance (Latvia)|National Alliance]] with four non-party ministers. Kulbergs pledged speed, plain language and responsibility.

Under PM Luca Niculescu, the opposition PNL and USR filed a motion against the health minister, debated on 25 Nov. After the Berlin coalition meeting, President [[p:Nicușor Dan]] said Romania would contribute more to financing and arming Ukraine in 2027 (translated). The Commission partly approved Romania's fifth recovery-plan payment of €2.67bn.
items.notes: Also: emergency services chief Raed Arafat sent to trial over a helicopter purchase. Niculescu government approved in October.

items.text: PM [[p:Rumen Radev]]'s cabinet tabled the 2027 budget with a 3.5% of GDP deficit target (4.2% with extra defence spending), calling it the most social budget in years. His party's majority makes passage likely.
Italy's 2027 budget timetable slipped after a record of about 6,600 amendments, over 2,000 from governing parties. Committee votes may start 12 Dec, with final approval targeted for 27–29 Dec.
PM [[p:Andrej Babiš]] attended the Berlin coalition-of-the-willing meeting; his cabinet left undecided whether to extend fuel-price regulation beyond the end of November.
items.notes: Earlier (11 Nov) Czechia opted out of a UK/French-led exercise in Poland; President Pavel criticised that.
